title: Il passato prossimo con essere
summary: Passato prossimo with essere for motion/change verbs, plus participle agreement

blocks.title: When the participle dresses like an adjective
blocks.body: Some verbs — especially **motion** or **change** verbs (*andare, partire, arrivare, tornare, nascere, morire*) — take **essere**, not avere. With essere, the participle **agrees** with the subject, just like an adjective: *sono andat**o*** (a man says this), *sono andat**a*** (a woman says this).
blocks.callout: Essere + participle → the participle's ending changes with gender and number.

blocks.title: One verb, four endings
blocks.body: Watch how the participle's final vowel changes depending on who's speaking.

items.en: I went to the sea. (a man)
I went to the sea. (a woman)

blocks.prompt: Sofia, about herself: 'I went to Milano.' Which is correct?
blocks.explain: *Andare* takes essere, and Sofia is a woman — the participle agrees: *andata*.

blocks.prompt: Which verbs usually take essere in the passato prossimo?
options: Motion and change-of-state verbs (andare, partire, diventare)
blocks.explain: Essere goes with motion, change of state, and (as you'll see next) reflexive verbs.

pairs.left: *Marco è andato al bar.* — Marco went to the bar (sing., masc.)
pairs.right: *Giulia e Sofia sono andate al bar.* — Giulia and Sofia went to the bar (pl., fem.)
pairs.note: The participle follows the subject: gender and number, every time.

blocks.prompt: Type 'I arrived' the way a woman would say it.
blocks.explain: *Sono arrivata* — arrivare takes essere, feminine singular agreement.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.

blocks.scene: Marco tells Giulia about his weekend, then she asks You too

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.en: I went to the sea on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.en: Really? Did you get back Sunday evening?
lines.spotlight: sei tornato — essere + participle agreeing masculine, since it's addressed to Marco.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.target: E tu? Hai visitato qualche posto questo weekend?
lines.en: And you? Did you visit anywhere this weekend?

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: No, ho lavorato tutto il weekend.

lines.speaker: Marco
lines.target: Ah, peccato! La prossima volta vieni con noi.
lines.en: Ah, too bad! Next time you're coming with us.

blocks.prompt: Write 2-3 sentences about somewhere you went recently, using essere + a participle with the correct agreement.
